hero.headline: Why can’t we just be friends?
hero.lead: Texans for a Safe Israel stands with the Jewish people in their God-given homeland — especially Jerusalem, Judea, and Samaria — and educates in Texas by building friendships without a hidden agenda.
hero.imageAlt: The TFSI lodge in Granbury with Texas and Israeli flags over the entrance

mission.title: A connector for the Jewish people
body: TFSI’s greatest role has been as a connector. Guests from the Biblical Heartland sit in a Texas house and tell their own story. Donors then fund the needs those friendships make visible: security, survivors, soldiers, and the next generation of visitors.

In Texas we educate through respectful relationships where real friendships can thrive. Most of the Christians who come through the house have never been to Israel and have never known a Jewish person. The guests change that.
mission.imageAlt: An Israeli flag hanging inside the log lodge in Granbury

work.title: The work
work.intro: Named people, named places, named items. These are the areas TFSI funds and the friendships behind them.

items.title: Critical needs
items.summary: When a community or family asks for help, TFSI moves quickly — drones, appliances, medical bags, or the specific item that keeps people safe.

items.title: Holocaust survivors
items.summary: Practical care without an agenda: appliances, home repairs, grocery cards at the holidays, and the things that restore dignity late in life.

items.title: Security and tactical supplies
items.summary: After October 7, funding for drones, vests, cameras, helmets, boots, jackets, and medical kits for communities in Judea and Samaria.

items.title: Soldiers and families
items.summary: Food and drink for battalions in the field, and support for widows, orphans, and traumatized children through trusted Israeli partners.

items.title: Hosting and education
items.summary: Israeli guests tell their own story in Texas living rooms. Friendships, not talking points.

items.title: Influencer trips
items.summary: First-hand travel to the Heartland so younger Americans meet the people and the land, not a headline.

items.title: The Biblical Highway
items.summary: A long-term effort to see Route 60 known worldwide as Israel’s national Biblical Highway — rest stops, overlooks, and real tourism in the Holy Cities.

items.title: Texas–Israel Embassy
items.summary: A working embassy concept: Texans in Israel and Israelis in Texas, with guides, business connections, and a place people can actually go.

jse.title: The Judea and Samaria Experience
jse.body: Personalized travel guidance for people who want to walk the land and meet the people who live there. Not a tour company. One conversation, then a match with trusted guides and hosts.
jse.imageAlt: Two travelers on a hilltop overlooking the Judean hills

quote.text: To Jews and to Christians we simply say: why can’t we just be friends?

closing.title: Stand with the people of the Heartland
closing.body: Every gift goes through Texans for a Safe Israel, a U.S. 501(c)(3). It keeps the house able to answer the next call from Arugot, Itamar, Shiloh, or a survivor in Texas.

hero.headline: What sets us apart
hero.lead: For more than a decade the house in Granbury has hosted the pioneers of Israel — most of them from Judea and Samaria. An interested group gathers. God’s covenant people tell the story of living out biblical prophecy in the land.
hero.imageAlt: An Israeli flag hanging inside the TFSI lodge

story.title: Friendships that fund the work
body: Those stories come with sacrifice, opposition, and immediate needs. That is the work: stand with the Jewish people, serve them, and take part in what is happening in the land.

President Ann Stacy has hosted Orthodox Jewish guests since October 2011. Texans for a Safe Israel was formed as a 501(c)(3) in 2018–2019 so those friendships could fund security projects and Holocaust education — not just conversation.
Mike Isley, founder of Texans for Israel, serves as vice president. The lodge flies Texas and Israeli flags over the same door for a reason.

list.name: Rabbi Shlomo Abrams
list.summary: A Dallas rabbi who teaches Torah, hosts events, and leads tours to Israel with his wife.
story: He is one of the sweetest young rabbis you will ever meet. He is associated with the Dallas Area Torah Association and is a pulpit rabbi with his own shul. When I am honored to talk to him, I always learn a little Torah that applies to the day.

I am forever grateful for him hosting Deputy Mayor Arieh King (who wasn’t Deputy Mayor at the time). He opened his shul and has offered to help on other occasions. His Jewish Learning Center is dedicated to bringing the beauty, warmth, and joy of Jewish learning to Jewish people of all Jewish backgrounds and affiliations.

Rabbi Shlomo takes a Jewish men’s tour to Israel each year while Hudi, his wife, watches the children, and then she takes Jewish women to Israel, and Rabbi Shlomo watches the children. I asked her once what she did with her newborns, and she said, “I take them with me!”

list.name: Rabbi Yosef Abrams
list.summary: Father of Rabbi Shlomo Abrams. Torah lessons on why Jews and Christians must close the gap between communities.
story: Once, Rabbi Shlomo Abrams called me and asked if he could bring his twins (he has two sets) to the Lake for an overnight stay. We were honored to have them. He told me he was bringing me a present... it was his dad, and he was true to his word. Rabbi Yosef was a gift from heaven to me. As the kids played, we talked and talked, and I learned so much.

Rabbi Abrams asked me a curious question. “Ann, are there actually more Christians like you who welcome the Jewish people as friends and have no agenda on their part but friendship?” If you are a Christian reading this, our behavior toward the Jewish people has been most shameful. It still amazes me that Jewish people think that someone like that is rare. We both have the same problem: Christians don’t know serious Jewish people, and serious Jewish people don’t know Christians.

After that visit, Rabbi Yosef Abrams taught his family Torah lessons from the Psalms, and I was included on Zoom. I counted that a great honor. When Americans for a Safe Israel went to Jerusalem in May 2019, Rabbi arranged for us to have a Five Star tour of Aish HaTorah. We had a beautiful lunch, and Rabbi Yosef Abrams taught the history of Jerusalem. It was also Jerusalem Day!

list.name: Rabbi Leo Dee
list.affiliation: Author, The Seven Facets of Healing
list.summary: Hosted in April 2026. His wife Lucy and daughters Maia and Rina were murdered by Hamas terrorists in April 2023. Author of The Seven Facets of Healing.
story: It was a great honor to host Rabbi Leo Dee in our home this past April (2026). We learned that he had worked as a financial analyst and investor in England before making aliyah to Israel with his family in 2014 and pursuing his rabbinical studies.

In April 2023, his life was forever changed when his beloved wife, Lucy, and two of their daughters, Maia and Rina, were brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists as they traveled to Tiberias for a Passover holiday. In the face of unimaginable loss, Rabbi Dee has demonstrated extraordinary courage and a determination to help others find healing and hope.

A published author, one of his books, The Seven Facets of Healing, offers a framework for those navigating trauma, personal loss, illness, conflict, or disappointment. His message is that we can begin to build a new world where resilience and hope grow alongside the positive memories we continue to cherish.

On a personal note, I am especially grateful to Rabbi Dee for opening his home to my grandson in 2024, along with twelve other young Christian bridge-builders (a trip sponsored by Israel365). His willingness to welcome and invest in these young people is a beautiful example of the understanding and relationships we hope to foster between Christians and Jews. I am deeply thankful for his generosity and for the opportunity to know him.

list.name: Rabbi Chaim Eisen
list.summary: Founder and dean of Yeshivath Sharashim – Zion Bible Studies. A speaker for four decades and a longtime mentor in Jewish–Christian friendship.
story: Rabbi Chaim Eisen is the founder and dean of Yeshivath Sharashim – Zion Bible Studies. An acclaimed speaker, he has been stimulating audiences throughout Israel, North America, and Europe for four decades. Over the past two decades, he has become increasingly engaged in building bridges between Jewish and Christian believers.

Nearly ten years ago, I met Rabbi Eisen in the most unexpected place—inside the tack barn of an exotic deer ranch! We became friends that day, and over the years, he has become a mentor to me. I have learned so much from his wisdom, his gracious spirit, and his ability to encourage Jews and Christians to respect our differences while recognizing how much unites us.

One of the things I love most about Rabbi Eisen is his heart for bringing people together without asking either side to compromise who they are. He reminds us that friendship, mutual respect, and a willingness to learn from one another can build lasting relationships. I especially love the way he often prays, “May we stand shoulder to shoulder in our joint efforts.” To me, those words capture the heart of bridge-building—and the kind of friendship I have been blessed to share with him.

One last thing! When Rabbi Eisen first came to The Blessing, it was on the coldest day of the year, with a wind chill of zero. Yet more than 60 people came for lunch! I sent them this now-old video of Rabbi Eisen and Bob O’Dell, “How I Came to Respect You.” You can find it by searching YouTube for “Bob O’Dell Chaim Eisen How I Came to Respect You.”

list.name: Rabbi Yishai Fleisher
list.summary: International spokesperson for the Jewish Community of Hebron, commentator, and podcast host. He and Malkah held their wedding in Hebron during the Second Intifada.
story: Many years ago, I regularly listened to Israel National News, Arutz Sheva, where I was introduced to Religious Zionist personalities. At the time, I might not have known how to identify myself with the term Religious Zionist, but I certainly identified with their message and the content they shared. One young man I especially enjoyed listening to was Rabbi Yishai Fleisher.

One year, I had the opportunity to hear him speak in Hebron during the Shabbaton of Chayei Sarah. He won my heart when he shared that he and Malkah had chosen Hebron as the place for their wedding. This was during the Second Intifada, when very few people were coming to Hebron. As I remember Yishai telling the story, he called the Gutnick Center in Hebron to ask whether the date they had chosen for their wedding was available. The man on the other end was apparently astonished. The center had been empty for the past two years!

Eventually, although I can no longer remember exactly how it came about, Yishai, Malkah, and their children began visiting us at The Blessing during the summers. Those visits became a special connection in our lives. In fact, the large Israeli flag hanging in our living room is a retired flag from Hebron, a meaningful reminder of our love for this remarkable community and the people who have become part of our story.

There is so much more to say about Yishai! I encourage you to begin by searching for Yishai Fleisher on YouTube and listening to him for yourself. Yishai has become a prominent voice in Israeli public life. He serves as an international spokesperson for the Jewish Community of Hebron, is a political commentator and podcast host, and has worked as an adviser and English-language spokesperson for Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s Minister of National Security. At the time of this writing (October 2026), Yishai is seeking a seat in the Knesset with Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power), the party led by Ben-Gvir.

For me, however, Yishai is more than a public figure or political voice. I remember the young man who chose to celebrate his wedding in Hebron at a time when so few others were willing to come. That decision spoke volumes about his heart, his convictions, and his commitment to the Jewish community in the Biblical heartland of Israel. It is a privilege to have known him and to have welcomed his family to The Blessing.

list.name: Rabbi Yehuda Glick
list.summary: Religious Zionist leader and former Knesset member. Stayed in the home three times. Amitsim, headed with Hadass Glick, works with young widows and orphans.
story: One of the brightest luminaries in the Religious Zionist movement. As a Knesset Member, he came to speak to our AFSI group one night. As others crowded around to get a picture, I was too intimidated by his presence to approach him. As life has turned out, he has stayed with us three times, and we have had our own personal discussions at the dinner table.

I have to smile as the Chief of Police in Jerusalem said he was the most dangerous man in the Middle East. Even heaven has to smile at that! He continually advocates for the right for Jews to pray on The Temple Mount and for all nations to have that right.

God has been so good to us to allow us to host him and, more recently, Hadass and him. I feel like royalty has come to Granbury! He is visionary for seeing Isaiah 56:7 come to pass... “My house shall be called a House of Prayer for all nations.”
list.photoAlt: Rabbi Yehuda Glick seated in the lodge

list.name: Rabbi Rami Goldberg
list.summary: Director of Strategic Relationships at Israel365 and host of the Biblical Money podcast. Has spoken at Generations Church.
story: Rabbi Rami Goldberg has been a guest in our home and a speaker at Generations Church. He serves as Director of Strategic Relationships at Israel365 and hosts the Biblical Money podcast. We hosted him for a luncheon several years ago, and I continue to stay in touch with him regularly through WhatsApp.

When Rabbi Rami spoke at Generations Church, he shared the moving story of his family and the terrible losses they suffered in the Holocaust. His father’s parents were Holocaust survivors, making his own family’s history especially poignant.

Yet out of this history, there is a beautiful story of bringing hope and joy to others. Rami’s father became Sabobo the Clown, a medical clown who brings laughter and comfort to children in Israeli hospitals. Imagine going from Wall Street to the hospital rooms of sick children, using humor and compassion.

list.name: Rabbi Moshe and Leah Goldsmith
list.summary: Close friends. Rabbi Goldsmith, then mayor of Itamar, guided a visit to the Fogel family home. Subsequent visits showed the daily reality of those communities.
story: Very close family friends! The terrible massacre of the Fogel Family in Itamar prompted me to call Americans for a Safe Israel and ask, “are you going to Itamar?” I had no idea what was waiting for me there, but, for sure, it was one of the greatest personal Divine Appointments.
Rabbi Moshe Goldsmith met our AFSI group and escorted us to the Fogel home. I picked a flower from Ruth Fogel’s struggling little garden. It is framed and in our living room in Texas.

In November, I returned to Israel with AFSI to accompany the whole town to the top of the hill where a new community was being developed. These young brave souls had come to establish a community between Itamar and Hawara. Unfortunately, the Army destroyed it ten days later due to pressure from the U.S.

Hawara is the Arab village on the Biblical Highway, Route 60, where the terrorist had come from. In February 2023, terrorists from this town murdered two young men from Har Bracha (home of the Waller Family and HaYovel).

list.name: Rabbi Richard Green
list.summary: Co-founder of The Clarion Project, focused on extremist threats.
story: Rabbi Richard Green is the co-founder of The Clarion Project, an independent nonprofit dedicated to helping the public understand, recognize, and reduce the growing threat of violent extremism both online and in our communities.

We met Richard long before there was a TFSI. He had moved to Dallas and was working hard at building relationships. In the early days, over a decade ago, we used to tell him... “we’ll leave the light on and lock the door behind you.” Fox News often uses reports from The Clarion Project. We love Richard and his family.

list.name: Rabbi Eitan Kupietzky
list.summary: Director of The Gimmel Foundation, which serves children, families, and new immigrants in disadvantaged Israeli communities. Has visited The Blessing twice.
story: Rabbi Eitan Kupietzky is the Director of The Gimmel Foundation, which serves disadvantaged communities in Israel. We were introduced through his brother, Rabbi Chanan Kupietzky, who is connected with the Temple Institute and the Red Heifers. I remember asking Rabbi Eitan if he had ever spoken to a Christian group. His answer was no, but at his brother’s encouragement, he was willing to step into unfamiliar territory and join us at The Blessing. I am so glad he did! We have now had the joy of welcoming him twice, and each visit has been a special opportunity to get to know him better and hear about the meaningful work to which he has devoted himself. There is something especially rewarding about watching a new relationship grow when people are willing to step beyond what is familiar and discover how much they can learn from one another.

The Gimmel Foundation, founded by Rabbi Eitan’s grandfather, is dedicated to educating and empowering children, families, new immigrants, and other vulnerable populations to overcome economic challenges, limited municipal support, and struggling schools. Its programs emphasize self-help and community involvement, offering practical support that helps individuals and families build stronger futures. Among its many initiatives are after-school educational clubs, mentoring and tutoring in local schools and community centers, holiday food and clothing distributions, summer day camps, and home visits by teachers and tutors. These are more than programs; they are personal investments in the lives of people who need encouragement, opportunity, and a helping hand.

There are so many worthy organizations serving the people of Israel, and choosing where to give can be difficult. But if Rabbi Eitan’s story and the work of The Gimmel Foundation touch your heart, I encourage you to reach out to him and learn more.

For me, the relationship with Rabbi Eitan is about more than introducing our friends to a worthy organization. It is about the friendships that grow when Christians and Jewish people open their homes, share their stories, and discover a common desire to make a difference. Rabbi Eitan ventured into unfamiliar territory when he first came to The Blessing, and we have been blessed in return. Through The Gimmel Foundation, he is building hope within Israeli communities, one child, one family, and one life at a time.

list.name: Rabbi Yitzchak Mamo
list.affiliation: The Third Temple and the Red Heifers
list.summary: Connected to the work toward the Third Temple and the Red Heifers. A friend for nearly ten years and an overnight guest at The Blessing.
story: I first met Rabbi Mamo at a ranch near Granbury, Texas, close to ten years ago. Over time, I came to know him better through his good friend, Byron Stinson, and our connection has continued to grow. A few years ago, Rabbi Mamo spent the night with us at The Blessing, and as I have learned over the years, sharing our home has a special way of cementing friendships and trust.

Rabbi Mamo is someone to follow if you are interested in the building of the Third Temple and the Red Heifers. He is connected to these fascinating topics, which bring together biblical prophecy, Jewish tradition, and the future of Israel.

I am always grateful for the opportunities The Blessing provides to turn acquaintances into friends and to build bridges with people whose work helps others better understand the land, the people, and the biblical heritage of Israel. There are a number of YouTube videos featuring Rabbi Mamo; one I found interesting is on BeardedBibleBros.com.

list.name: Rabbi Tuly Weisz
list.summary: Founder of Israel365, author of Universal Zionism, and publisher of The Israel Bible. TFSI supports Israel365 monthly.
story: Rabbi Tuly Weisz is the founder of Israel365, author of Universal Zionism, and publisher of the best-selling The Israel Bible, which highlights the special relationship between the Land of Israel and the People of Israel.

Years ago, we had the privilege of spending a wonderful Shabbaton with Rabbi Tuly and Rabbi Eli Mischel. I believe that gathering was a pivotal moment in cementing friendships between a small group of Jews and Christians in the DFW Area. Those relationships have meant so much to us, and from that night stronger relationships have developed.

As it happened, that Sunday was July 4th. Rabbi Tuly had a few hours to spare and stopped by our home! With the holiday and such short notice, I could only gather a small group, but we were delighted to have him. I remember thinking, “One day, we will proudly say, ‘Rabbi Tuly Weisz came to our home we call The Blessing.’”

My appreciation for Rabbi Tuly and his work has only grown. I buy The Israel Bible by the carton because I love sharing it with others. TFSI supports Israel365 on a monthly basis. We believe deeply in their mission and the important work they do to strengthen the connection between people around the world and the Land and People of Israel. Israel365 is a VERY WORTHY organization, and we are honored to support them!

list.name: Pastor Rafael Cruz
list.summary: A survivor of oppression in Cuba and a close family friend. Father of Senator Ted Cruz.
story: He has become family to us. We actually met him at a Shabbat dinner of Diane and Jerry Benjamin’s. Since then, he has been our guest when he preaches in our area. Words cannot express his great personal blessing to our family, our children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.

He is the American Dream personified. Born in Cuba, he lived a life as a teenager under the oppressive regime of the dictator Batista. He began to fight the regime but was imprisoned and tortured. A miracle story is how he arrived in Texas in 1957 on a student visa, not speaking English, with only $50.00 sewn into his underwear by his mother.

He got a job as a dishwasher making 50 cents an hour but quickly moved up to a short-order cook. He has a wonderful story of how he learned to crack two eggs in one hand. He has demonstrated his expertise at breakfast on our stovetop!

There is so much to his story, but the fact is God had a call on his life and, through his life, a call on his son’s life, Senator Ted Cruz. His call is for pastors to return their pulpits to America’s Biblical and Historical foundations.

list.name: Pastor Juana Earley
list.summary: Pastor of The Glory Church, 65 miles from Granbury, which hosts many of the same Israeli guests who visit The Blessing. A retired surgical nurse.
story: I have known Juana for many years. A retired surgical nurse by profession, she has long been active in evangelism to the Nations and recently returned from a trip to the Yucatán. Juana was also deeply involved in supporting Israel and the Jewish people through the Battalion of Deborah (see Keith and Jodi Anderson).

After her husband, Pastor Bill Earley, passed away a few years ago, Juana became the full-time pastor of The Glory Church. She has been a tremendous help to me personally and to TFSI, generously hosting some of the same remarkable Israelis who visit us here in Granbury.

Juana is a true bridge-builder between Christians and the Jewish people. Just 65 miles from Granbury, The Glory Church has become an extension of the hospitality we offer at The Blessing, allowing another community of Christians to meet Israelis face-to-face, hear their personal stories, and develop relationships that might never have begun otherwise. These encounters move beyond simply supporting Israel from a distance; they give people the opportunity to know the Jewish people personally, understand their lives and experiences, and build lasting friendships.

I am especially grateful that Juana has helped TFSI extend its reach in this way. What began in our home now reaches another congregation through her generosity and commitment. Juana understands that building bridges is not just about speaking up for Israel; it is about bringing people together, creating meaningful connections, and allowing friendships to grow between Christians and the Jewish people. Her partnership has helped make that possible.

list.name: Pastor Alan Latta
list.summary: Pastor of Generations Church in Granbury. Has welcomed Israelis to speak at his church.
story: Pastor Alan Latta is one of my favorite pastors, firmly grounded in the Word of God and a dear friend to us and our Jewish guests. Pastor Alan has joined us on our journey at The Blessing, our family home, where we welcome Israelis to share their stories. Sometimes I feel as though our home has become a modern-day version of Longfellow’s Tales of a Wayside Inn, a place where people gather and stories bring us closer together.

Pastor Alan has taken that spirit beyond our home by welcoming Israelis to speak at his church, becoming a bridge builder between Christians and our Jewish brothers and sisters. You can also find him featured in interviews on Root-Source.com, alongside other Christian pastors who are extending a hand of genuine friendship to the Jewish people.
We are grateful for his friendship and for the example he sets. If you are a Christian looking for a great church, you will find a home at Generations Church, Granbury, Texas.

list.name: Pastor John Turner
list.summary: Leads the Father’s House Foundation. A mentor when TFSI first began organizing trips to Israel.
story: Pastor John Turner is a wonderful man who has been a blessing to our community and to Texans For A Safe Israel. He has a deep and abiding love for Israel and the Jewish people, a passion that has been evident in his support and encouragement over the years.

A number of years ago, Byron and Tammy Stinson entrusted their Father’s House Foundation to his leadership. John was also a tremendous mentor to me when we first began organizing TFSI trips to Israel. His wisdom, encouragement, and guidance were invaluable as we took those early steps.
He has continued to support us by attending many of our events, and I am grateful for his friendship and his heart for Israel and the Jewish people.

list.name: Knesset Member Ohad Tal
list.summary: Member of the Knesset for the Religious Zionist Party. Spoke at The Blessing in September 2025.
story: Knesset Member Ohad Tal was with us at The Blessing in September 2025. He is an Israeli politician and a Member of the Knesset representing the Religious Zionist Party. Ohad believes that peace can only be achieved by applying Israeli sovereignty over Judea and Samaria and Gaza. You can check with virtually every guest we have welcomed into our home from Judea and Samaria, and they will tell you the same.

Although I am not Jewish or Israeli, after so many years of personal relationships with the people who live in the Biblical Heartland, I have come to understand their deep connection to this land. My convictions have grown through the people I have met, the stories they have shared, and the friendships that have developed over the years.

We had seven overnight guests the evening Ohad spoke. That is part of what makes The Blessing so special. We don’t simply invite people to speak to us; we welcome them into our home, share meals, and have the opportunity to get to know them personally. The conversations around our breakfast table the next morning are often just as meaningful as the formal gathering the evening before.

This is what TFSI has been about for so many years—building bridges between Christians and the Jewish people through personal relationships, hospitality, and a desire to understand the people who call Judea and Samaria home.

list.name: Joshua Aaron
list.summary: An impromptu concert in Granbury arranged in a single day. Nearly 400 people attended.
story: I don’t think he will ever forget Granbury, Texas! It was very early on a Monday morning when Lori Hinze excitedly called me to say that he was in the U.S. and she thought we should arrange a concert at our home. I barely knew who he was at the time, although I soon discovered that he was VERY popular! I had briefly seen a video of him performing in Jerusalem before a very large audience, but I had no idea what was about to unfold.

One miracle after another seemed to fall into place. He had not planned to come to Texas, but we discovered that if he left the Carolinas very early Sunday morning, connected through Atlanta, and caught a Dallas-bound flight, he could arrive by noon that same day! The largest church in Granbury generously offered its facilities for the afternoon at no charge. A woman we barely knew stepped forward to pay his honorarium, and others pitched in to fill whatever gaps remained.
We thought we would be fortunate to have 100 people attend, but nearly 400 showed up! That evening, we hosted him, along with 30 other guests, for a lovely dinner in our home.

Looking back, it is hard not to marvel at how everything came together. What began with an unexpected phone call became an extraordinary gathering, made possible by the generosity and willingness of so many people to step forward. Yes, this was an impromptu meeting and connection we will never forget, and I suspect Granbury, Texas, will always hold a special place in his memory, too!

list.name: Keith and Jodi Anderson
list.summary: Pioneers in Christian–Jewish relations. There would be no Texans for a Safe Israel without them.
story: All I can say is there would be no Texans for a Safe Israel if not for this amazing pioneer couple dedicated to bettering Christian-Jewish relations.

I met Jodi over the phone in 2014, a few weeks before David Wilder arrived. Little did either of us know the tragedy coming. She lost their son a few days after that. Just two weeks after that, the doctors gave her a grim diagnosis. Nevertheless, she never stopped doing everything she could with every ounce of breath left in her for Israel, Judea, Samaria, and the Jewish People wherever she found them.

Keith always was in the background making sure details were attended to. It took them both! They led countless group trips to Israel, sharing all the time about their Covenant friends and the Promises of God to them. She was my mentor, cheerleader, and good friend to me. To say she has been sorely missed is a gross understatement. There is not a day I don’t think about her.

Keith has since passed away. As I said, he was always behind the scenes, but Jodi could never have done what she did without him. I have no words for the personal blessing he was to our family. He never gave up on one of our children... ever the encourager, and he saw tremendous fruit come from that work.

list.name: Gidon Ariel
list.summary: Founder of Root Source, built for Jewish–Christian dialogue, study, and lasting relationships.
story: I have the warmest feelings when I think of our good friend Gidon. He is family also. He has been to The Blessing many times. He is the best connector I know. He has the ability to schmooze like none other! He is just comfortable with everyone. People love him. I love him.

His idea of Root-Source was a pioneering effort along with Bob O’Dell. He has put authentic, knowledgeable, and loving Jewish teachers together with “curious” pro-Israel Christians, Christians who have begun to wonder about the roots of their Christian faith. Gidon’s heart was dedicated to promoting respectful relationships between Christians and Jews. Eventually, Root-Source was born.

Just a few years ago, the idea of Jews and Christians studying together to concentrate on the Hebrew Scripture and Jewish Wisdom would have been impossible and unimaginable. Gidon is a true pioneer. Initially, it seemed he was tilling the rockiest ground with a wooden shovel, but with his persistence, Root-Source has grown by leaps and bounds.

list.name: Ayala Bar-On
list.summary: Head of the Foreign Desk and International Spokesperson for the Har Hevron (Southern Hebron Hills) Regional Council. Visited The Blessing in June 2025.
story: Ayala Bar-On came to The Blessing in June 2025, at the same time as Ruthy Mann. Ayala is a beautiful young woman with an important responsibility as Head of the Foreign Desk and International Spokesperson for the Har Hevron Regional Council, also known as the Southern Hebron Hills Regional Council. She has a big job—building international partnerships and connecting the Hills of Hebron with people around the world.

Ayala is a familiar voice in international discussions about Israel and Judea and Samaria. She is frequently featured on programs, podcasts, and media discussions, including Live the Land and our own The Judea and Samaria Experience podcast, sponsored by Texans for a Safe Israel (TFSI). Through these conversations, she helps introduce global audiences to the history, development, and biblical significance of this remarkable region—the heartland of Israel.

I am grateful that TFSI has had the opportunity to welcome Ayala into our home and help share the stories of those who live and work in the biblical heartland. Building bridges is about more than bringing people together; it is about helping others see the land through the eyes of the people who call it home. Ayala does exactly that, helping the world understand the people, communities, and enduring connections that make the Hills of Hebron so special.

list.name: Menachem Bar-Shalom
list.summary: Formerly with ZAKA; now works with Israel Magen Fund supporting Holocaust survivors in Ma'ale Adumim, including the piano given to a 90-year-old concert pianist.
story: Menachem is another family friend. I first met him through his position as American Fund Raiser for ZAKA, an Israeli first responder group that works internationally. In any global crisis, you will see ZAKA’s yellow jackets. We remained friends after his retirement.

He called me one day regarding Holocaust Survivors in Ma’ale Adumim, his community. There were 700 Survivors at the time, but about 150-160 needed additional help. Menachem’s parents were survivors, and he considered it a mitzvah to honor his parents with assistance to these people. He became trusted friends with a Russian social service lady named Mariana.

Menachem, Mariana, and I were able to help these mostly Russian and Ukrainian survivors with things the Israeli government did not provide. We gave funds for a couple of new air conditioners, a washer/dryer, deep freeze, supplemented rent payments, removed a tub and put in a shower for an elderly couple, several medical and therapy procedures, a computer, glasses, iPad, and even something as small as a bread maker. However, my favorite was a piano for a 90-year-old former concert pianist. I struggled with this as it seemed extreme... Tehila Gimpel helped me with this. What she said changed the way I look at giving.

He is now working with David Rose and Israel Magen Fund, raising funds for security vehicles, cameras, drones, etc., for the Binyamin Region of Israel. Menachem has become one of my Jewish mentors, an all-around good friend, and a partner in helping the Holocaust Survivors in Ma’ale Adumim.

list.name: Moshe Bar Zvi
list.summary: Former president of the Jerusalem Post and founder of Footsteps. Visited during the 2015 snowstorm and still filled the house.
story: A man I will never forget. It was Feb. 28, 2015, and DFW’s biggest snow day in a long time. I think it still holds the record for DFW this century. How do you get people to attend an event featuring someone they have never heard of? That is really a perennial challenge even today.

Early one morning, I began looking into any interview I could find. The result of that video was we had a full house even on that treacherous day! We had two different cars coming from Oklahoma that had to turn around as I-35 was closed. He was our last Israeli visitor to our Keller home. I don’t think any of us will ever forget that day.
He was more than an encourager to me. Moshe has quite a resume, as he was once the President and CEO of the Jerusalem Post and founder of Footsteps.

list.name: Sondra Oster Baras
list.summary: From Ohio, family since 2011. Bridges Christians and Jews from the Heartland with law and Torah teaching.
story: I first met her in 2011 when she and Dror Vanunu were our first Israeli Orthodox guests, or Religious Zionists. Sondra is another guest I count as family.

As Christians, it is hard for us to understand that there are many Jews that still believe all Christians are bad. We have given them substantial evidence of that for much of the last 2000 years. Just as 99% of Christians know no religious Jews, 99.9% of religious Jews know no committed Christians.

Sondra was raised in Ohio, graduated from Columbia Law School, and passed the bar in the U.S. and Israel. She and her husband live in Karnei Shomron, where for forty years, they have raised their family. You will not find a better advocate for the settler movement in Israel and for connecting Christians to Biblical Israel. The major part of the work for CFOIC is centered in Judea and Samaria.

You can ask Sondra any question, as she understands us sometimes better than we (Christians) understand ourselves. There are many videos for CFOIC, but an interesting one is FACING THE DIVIDE, a frank conversation between a Christian and a Jew. She also teaches a weekly Torah class that you will want to join.

list.name: Diane Benjamin and Jerry Benjamin
list.summary: TFSI’s first Jewish friends in the Dallas Jewish community. Diane led B’nai Zion for years; Jerry represents the Jewish War Veterans.
story: Diane and Jerry Benjamin were our first Jewish friends in the Dallas Jewish community, and what a blessing they have been! Anytime I have asked them to host someone, they have always been willing to help. They have even made the trek down to Granbury a few times to visit us!

Diane has been affectionately called the “Unofficial Mayor of Dallas,” and I can certainly understand why. Through Diane, TFSI was introduced to leaders in the Dallas Jewish community, and many lasting friendships began. She is legendary for her Shabbat dinners, and it was at one of those dinners that I met my now longtime friend, Rafael Cruz.

Diane led B’nai Zion, a charitable organization, for a number of years, raising millions of dollars in support of B’nai Zion Hospital in Israel. Her commitment to the Jewish community and to Israel is truly remarkable. Jerry has proudly represented the Jewish War Veterans, another worthy organization. Diane is also actively involved in conservative politics, both at the state level and in Dallas.

On a personal note, Diane has been my mentor in “all things Jewish!” I have learned so much from her, and I am grateful for the doors she has opened, the friendships she has helped cultivate, and the generosity she and Jerry have shown us over the years. Some friendships become part of the very fabric of your life and ministry. Diane and Jerry are certainly that kind of friends to us. I love Diane and Jerry, and I thank God for bringing them into our lives!

list.name: Lorrie Cardoza Moore
list.summary: Christian activist, film producer, and longtime host of Focus on Israel. TFSI donates to her organization.
story: Lorrie Cardoza Moore is not only a dear friend of TFSI, but also a woman whose passion for Israel, the Jewish people, and our nation’s Judeo-Christian heritage I deeply admire. She is a Christian activist, film producer, and longtime host of Focus on Israel, a television program that has educated Christian audiences about Israel for many years.

Lorrie has also been a national leader in working with school boards to restore the traditional American and Judeo-Christian values that helped shape our nation. Just this past June, she was instrumental in the Texas State Board of Education’s efforts to incorporate traditional American conservative values into our schools. Perhaps you know that 27 states look to Texas for leadership in textbook decisions, making this work especially significant.

Although Lorrie and I share a deep love for Israel and the Jewish people, much of our work has taken different paths. I suspect she may be even better known in Israel than she is here in the United States because of her tireless efforts to speak the truth about Israel and defend the Jewish people.
I am thankful for Lorrie’s friendship and deeply appreciate the courage and dedication she brings to the causes we both hold so dear. We are donors to her organization.

list.name: Bill Cloud
list.summary: A Christian minister who teaches shared Hebraic roots. Based in Cleveland, Tennessee.
story: Although we are Christians, most of our guests have been Orthodox. Bill is a Christian minister who loves Israel and the Jewish people and works from the Christian side to be a bridge builder to the Jewish people. He accomplishes this by educating Christians about our shared Hebraic Roots.

His wonderful and very talented family resides in Cleveland, Tennessee. You could reach him through Shoreshim Ministries. He is a fabulous teacher regarding Hebraic Roots! I had admired his teaching on TV long before I had the honor of meeting him.

list.name: Chaplain Ruthann Crosby
list.summary: A teacher who opens up Jewish Scripture for Christians. Two TFSI board members have flown to Alaska to learn from her.
story: We are a small group of people who are deeply committed to building bridges of understanding and friendship with the Jewish people. Somehow, people with like hearts find one another, and when Ruthann found us, our hearts immediately bonded.

Ruthann has a remarkable gift for opening doors of understanding and revealing perspectives within Jewish Scripture (the Old Testament) that many Christians have never considered. She helps us see familiar passages through new eyes, bringing deeper meaning and understanding to the Scriptures. We are so grateful for her ability to articulate the many mysteries and profound insights found within Jewish Scripture in a way that can truly change your life forever.

Her teaching has made such an impact that two of our TFSI board members have even flown to her home in Alaska to learn more! Ruthann is a treasured friend and teacher, and we are thankful for the understanding she brings to those of us who desire to build meaningful, respectful relationships with the Jewish people.

list.name: Christine and Peter Darg
list.summary: Journalists and ministers in Israel since 1975. Christine is known for connecting with Orthodox Jews, Arabs, and Christians.
story: Perhaps best known today for The Jerusalem Channel and Exploits Ministry. We were flattered to host Christine and Peter through the friendship of Jodi and Keith Anderson.

Christine and Peter have been connected as journalists and in ministry in Israel since 1975. Theirs is such an extensive ministry, covering nearly 50 years, that I don’t know where to begin. Christine has friends within the Orthodox Jewish Community, the Arab Community, and the Christian Community... a rare ability few have.
I saw her at the Jerusalem Prayer Breakfast in Houston (February 2023), and seeing her was quite an honor!

list.name: Yigal Dilmoni
list.affiliation: Yesha Council / American Friends of Judea and Samaria
list.summary: CEO of the Yesha Council and founder of American Friends of Judea and Samaria. TFSI is working with him on support for farms in the region.
story: Yigal Dilmoni is the CEO of the Yesha Council, which, for us Texans, is somewhat like the governing voice of Judea and Samaria. TFSI first met Yigal in 2025 through our connection with the Israeli grassroots organization founded by Nadia Matar and Yehudit Katsover, which advocates for Jewish communities in Gaza, Judea, and Samaria.

Yigal and I met again at the Israel Forum last November. This week (October 2026), two TFSI board members are meeting with Yigal to discuss how we can best support the growth and development of farms in the region, including sheep and cattle operations and the provision of farm equipment and tractors.

Yigal is now also the founder and CEO of American Friends of Judea and Samaria, and it is a WONDERFUL ORGANIZATION! One of his greatest strengths is his exceptional ability to connect with people and build support for Israel through outreach. We look forward to welcoming him personally to The Blessing and continuing to build this important relationship.

list.name: Tim and Amy Eastwell
list.summary: A young family from Colorado Springs who livestream prayer from the Walls of Jerusalem. Joined by 50,000 people from more than 70 countries.
story: Tim and Amy Eastwell are just the greatest couple from Colorado Springs! As I write these words, I want you to understand that this is a young family with a dream, simply trying to respond to the Lord as faithfully as they know how.

In 2023, they were given a mandate to take people to Israel, organize prayer for Israel in Jerusalem, and invite the entire world to join them. God gave them the idea of livestreaming prayer from the Walls of Jerusalem on YouTube. And can you believe it? They were joined by 50,000 people from more than 70 countries!

I want to remind you that these are not seasoned professionals with a large organization behind them. They are a young family stepping out in faith, trusting the Lord to lead them as they go (and all the kids go with them!). You can learn more about their work at TheNarrowBridge.org. You can connect directly with Tim at Timeastwell@hotmail.com.

list.name: Daniel and Alana Elliot
list.summary: Certified sommeliers who import award-winning wines from the Golan Heights, Samaria, the Galilee, and the Elah Valley. Former guests at The Blessing.
story: Daniel and Alana Elliot are both certified sommeliers and the founders of Israeli Good Wine. They bring the very best of Israel’s wine country right to your door, importing and delivering high-quality, award-winning wines directly from vineyards in the Golan Heights, the hills of Samaria, the Galilee, and the Elah Valley.

Daniel and Alana have been guests in our home, and they are just a wonderful couple with a story worth hearing. If you are planning an Israel-related event, I encourage you to give them a call. What better way to bring a little taste of Israel to your gathering than with wines from the land itself?
Watch the short video on their About Us page to hear their story.

list.name: Ambassador Yoram Ettinger (Retd.)
list.summary: An expert in U.S.–Israel relations and a frequent guest. Known for humility and a love of music.
story: One of our favorites, but this list contains all favorites. We have never had anyone stay with us that was nothing but a delight. Any one of the people we have hosted would be a great guest speaker for you.

Ambassador Ettinger is an Israeli researcher, diplomat, writer, lecturer, and consultant to Israeli and US legislators and their staffers. He is an expert on US-Israel relations, Middle East affairs, and Jewish-Arab demography. You will want to sign up for his weekly Ettinger Report. There are more YouTube videos than you can count.

At one time, he was Consul General to the Southwest from Israel and learned to love our music! He is a forever friend, and one of the humblest men I have ever met. He spent some days with us in 2022, and one of our favorite times was taking him to 130-plus-year-old honky tonks in Bluff Dale, Texas. The surprise visit of an Ambassador from Israel made these two good ole boys’ days.

list.name: Tova Feldman
list.summary: A survivor who later came to Israel in 1949 and now lives in Arlington. Still teaches Hebrew.
story: One of my best friends. I met Tova through Jodi Anderson. When I found out she taught Hebrew, I signed up. That was nine years ago, and I could write a book about our sweet relationship. Tova is loved by so many. She is often the honored guest at any event. She is a very young Survivor. Her story, her family story, is a Miracle Story.

She is from Slovakia. Her dad was taken away first to a labor camp. Her mom had false papers that identified her as Hungarian. When they finally did come for her mom and the children, the first miracle was they took them to Novaky Work Camp, the very camp where her dad was a carpenter. When you read about the camp, you realize it was because of the timing of this camp that her family survived. However, three times they were on deportation lists and twice actually loaded on a train. Novaky was a building camp; they needed her dad’s carpentry ability, so they were removed.

In the late summer of 1944, the Partisans threw open the gates and said, “run for your lives!” Another miracle was the family stayed together as they began to run, but where do you run alone, much less with five little children? They stayed with a Christian family for a week or so, but there were so many of them, and food was in such shortage, they had to leave. It was also a death sentence to that family for helping Jews if they were found out. Tova feels nothing but kindness to that family for opening their home for the days they did.

Taking them away from the Camp was another miracle, as so many others were rounded up. They were walking down a road when a horse and wagon came along. The father asked, not for himself or his wife, if the children could ride on the wagon as they were so tired. The man agreed. Somewhere down the road, the father felt it was time to move into the forest. As they got to the edge of the forest, a plane came over bombing and obliterating the man, horse, and wagon. They were safe but by a hair’s breadth. Another Miracle!

They eventually found a concrete bunker deep in the forest. Her remembrance is that about twenty-two or twenty-three Jewish people were trying to hide. That is where they spent the Slovakian Winter. I asked what they ate, and she says, “potato peels, but Ann, that is where the nutrition is.” Another Miracle. She said she didn’t like what she had to eat but never felt hunger pangs. I asked how did they get even potato peels. She said the men, one at a time each day, would go and beg for food.

Another remembrance was a mom and a dad with a little boy her age and an infant. You can imagine the snowy forest and a baby’s cry. Tova says she remembers some of the adults grumbling over the infant crying. How many miracles there were probably couldn’t even be counted. Somehow they spent the entire winter there without being found out. My question still remains, how could you keep little children quiet? She doesn’t know, except it was something she just knew she had to do, not make a sound. Can you imagine? Four years old, and her sister was three. Certainly a Miracle.

Three weeks before the war ended, one man was captured and tortured. He told the Nazis their location. Even that man, she holds no ill will. She said, “what could he do when he was tortured?” The Nazis came in trucks and immediately started shooting. They killed the mother and the infant sibling of her little friend. Then another Miracle for her family: an officer stopped the killing. Those left alive were loaded onto trucks and taken to town, where they were locked in a school. Three weeks later, they unlocked the door and said, “the war is over; you can go home.” Tova was now five years old.

Her mom and dad never told their story to Tova, her brother, or her sisters. She said sometimes the children would hear them talking to their friends who had also been in the camps. Tova was the second to youngest of the family. Her older sisters and brother were able to add more information.

At five years of age, she remembers walking into their hometown. They were not treated well. The only question was, “how did you survive?” Their home was still there but stripped of all belongings, and nothing was ever returned. His carpentry shop no longer had any tools.

Eventually, they immigrated to Israel in 1949. Tova is a wealth of information about the earliest days of the State of Israel. They lived in immigrant housing crowded in with other families sharing a communal kitchen. One of her remembrances to me is the dances they would have that would bring everyone out to welcome new residents. Each time people would go with the hope of finding a long-lost relative or news of a family member that they didn’t know was alive or dead.

As I look at the 1945 Life Magazines and pictures from VE Day... the worldwide celebrations... the laughter, the kisses, the champagne... I think how bittersweet that day must have been to those Jewish People.

One last thing: Tova will not walk across the floor without her shoes. If you know anything about the Shoah, you know that having shoes meant the difference between life and death. The children were never... ever allowed to remove their shoes.

Tova is a great speaker. She still teaches Hebrew! She lives in Arlington in the greater Dallas Fort Worth Area. There is so much more to her story than I have written. Please contact me, and I will put you in contact with Tova. You will love her!

list.name: Jonathan Feldstein
list.summary: Connects Jews, Christians, and Israel through Run For Zion and the Genesis 123 Foundation.
story: Throughout three decades of work in non-profit PR, marketing, and fundraising, Jonathan has developed a unique and meaningful niche building bridges between Jews and Christians and Christians with Israel. He has taken this calling to new heights as President of Run for Zion and the Genesis 123 Foundation.

I met Jonathan through Mike Isley, and Mike told me he thought he was probably the most effective bridge builder he knew. As an Orthodox Jew, he is completely at ease in Christian circles. He is more than an engaging and delightful man.

His podcasts are becoming very popular. Because he interviewed one of the people on this list, I suggest you go to INSPIRATION FROM ZION JONATHAN FELDSTEIN and listen to the September 29th interview with Byron Stinson, The Return of the Red Heifer to Israel. (Byron and Tammy Stinson are our neighbors in Granbury. We can take a boat to each other’s home... how great is that!)

Jonathan is often in the U.S. and available for speaking engagements. He has promised to host a Shabbat dinner for us in Granbury, and we will hold him to it! Go to his website, Genesis 123 Foundation, for more information.

list.name: Jayne and Steve Foss
list.summary: Jayne is Southwest Director for Bridges for Peace. Steve often introduces speakers at events in Grapevine, Texas.
story: Steve and Jayne are two wonderful Christian friends who have blessed TFSI beyond measure. They have faithfully helped us spread the word about our events, sharing our heart for serving the Jewish people and standing with Israel. Steve is a gifted speaker with a deep appreciation for the restoration of Israel, and he often introduces speakers at events in Grapevine, Texas.

Jayne serves as Southwest Director for Bridges for Peace, a wonderful organization that works alongside Israel and the Jewish people. It has been a joy to see the connections grow between our ministries. Guests who visit us at The Blessing often become guests at Bridges for Peace events in Grapevine. What a blessing to share this common purpose with friends who are so committed to Israel and her people!

list.name: Helen Freedman
list.summary: Former AFSI director and mentor. A tireless advocate for Judea and Samaria.
story: Helen, of blessed memory, was the Director of AFSI for many years, but much more; she was my mentor and friend. There was no better spokesperson for the rights of the Jewish people to a Whole Israel, to Historic Israel, than Helen Freedman.

I once sent her the book The Butterfly Effect by Andy Andrews. It is a little history book on how seemingly one person can change the course of history. Through the years, I have probably purchased 150 of those little books. “The Butterfly Effect rests on the notion that the world is deeply interconnected, and one life can greatly influence a much larger complex.”

Helen spent most of her life fighting for Judea and Samaria. I believe with my heart that today’s groundswell of support for sovereignty for Judea and Samaria can be traced back to a few people, and Helen Freedman is one of those. There are many YouTube videos of Helen, including an interview David Wilder did on a visit when I was with her.

list.name: Benji Gershon
list.summary: Founder of American Jewish Conservatives. TFSI supports him every month.
story: Benji Gershon is the founder of American Jewish Conservatives, a grassroots organization committed to the enduring principles that have shaped our nation. They are fervently pro-God, pro-America, pro-Israel, and pro-Constitution.

I have known Benji for over a decade, and one of my favorite memories is the time I learned he would be in Jerusalem. I asked him, “If TFSI arranged a car and guide to take you through Judea and Samaria, would you go?” He and his wife were actually on their honeymoon, but they said yes! I believe that experience changed them forever.

Since then, Benji has welcomed a number of Israel’s rising stars to share their personal stories and bring Americans the truth about what is really happening in Israel. It is a privilege to see how that journey has grown into a meaningful connection between American Jewish conservatives and the people of Israel. We support him every month.

list.name: Jeremy and Tehila Gimpel
list.affiliation: Arugot Farm / Land of Israel Fellowship
list.summary: Pivotal in the Sovereignty Movement and in reaching Christians through the Land of Israel Fellowship. Their work at Arugot Farm in the Judean hills is one of TFSI’s closest partnerships.
story: Years ago, I saw two young men on a Jewish TV station. It was Jeremy Gimpel and Ari Abromowitz. I didn’t realize that they were in a circle of people that would end up including many of the people on this list. Helen Freedman, among others here, was on their Tuesday Night in Jerusalem show. You can still find some of those shows on YouTube.

Traveling with Americans for a Safe Israel, our paths would cross, and the Gimpels began to come to the U.S. for a month’s tour each year. Granbury became a stop. We have become a way station, a safe place to eat and rest on a long journey. We are at a crossroads for Texas and the U.S.; the DFW International airport is not so far away.

They are at the forefront of the Sovereignty Movement for Judea and Samaria. Their initiative of reaching out to Christians is unsurpassed with their Land of Israel Fellowship. There is wonderful work going on in the Judean hills. If you go to Israel, you must go to Arugot Farm!

list.name: Ephraim Goldsmith
list.summary: Son of Rabbi Moshe and Leah Goldsmith. Stayed for several weeks after his IDF service and remains close with the Stacy family.
story: Ephraim, along with his parents, Rabbi Moshe and Leah Goldsmith from Itamar, were among some of our very first guests at The Blessing. Many Israelis take time to travel and rest after completing their IDF service, and Ephraim stayed with us for several weeks.

During that time, he spent a great deal of time with our son and daughter-in-law, John Jr. and Brandee Stacy. Their son, our grandson John, was about Ephraim’s age, and the two young men quickly discovered they had much in common. Today, our grandson is a proud U.S. Marine, while Ephraim continues to serve in the IDF in an elite unit. Despite the miles between them, they remain good friends.

Eleven years have passed. That special connection between our families has continued through the years. A few years ago, Brandee traveled to Israel to attend Ephraim’s wedding, a beautiful reminder that the relationships formed in our home have grown far beyond those early visits.

What began as opening our home to a young Israeli and his family has become something truly special. We didn’t just welcome Ephraim and his parents, Rabbi Moshe and Leah Goldsmith, into The Blessing; we welcomed them into our family.

list.name: Rachel Greene
list.summary: Teaches emergency preparedness and self-sufficiency. A Zionist who travels the back roads of Judea and Samaria.
story: Rachel Greene is a gem! Years ago, I suggested that my daughter-in-law take Rachel’s class on emergency preparedness and self-sufficiency. You can learn more about her at ThePatriotNurse.com.

What we discovered was that Rachel was not only a gifted teacher but also an active Zionist who shares our love for Israel. Over the years, she has become much more than a teacher; she has become a dear friend to our entire family.

Rachel lives life with a spirit of adventure, traveling to Israel with nothing more than a backpack and exploring the back roads of Judea and Samaria. She is a woman of courage, conviction, and action, and we are blessed to call her our friend.

list.name: Eve Harow
list.affiliation: Rejuvenation With Eve Harow / Land of Israel Network
list.summary: Tour guide and veteran podcaster who knows Judea and Samaria and the people who live there. In the 1990s she camped on Dagan Hill to keep it from being given away, and she lives there today.
story: I first met Eve in November 2025, but it feels as though we have known each other our entire lives! I have long admired her work as a veteran podcaster on the Land of Israel Network, where she hosts Rejuvenation With Eve Harow. Eve is also one of Israel’s outstanding tour guides. What makes her so special is her ability to connect the past, present, and future at every stop. She knows Judea and Samaria like the back of her hand—not only its history and geography but, more importantly, the people who live there. Her close relationships with the residents bring the Biblical Heartland to life in a way few guides can. Eve guides with her Bible in hand! How many guides do that?

Eve returned to visit us this past August, and, as always, we had a wonderful time. There is so much to say about this remarkable woman, but here is one story you won’t want to miss! In the 1990s, when the Israeli government was considering giving away a hill near Eve’s community to the Arabs, Eve took action. With a nursing baby and four other courageous women, she went to the hill and camped out there. The struggle that followed even landed Eve in jail—with her baby! But here is the extraordinary ending: Eve lives on that very hill today! You can read the story in Israel365’s “The Women Who Saved Dagan Hill.” It tells you something about Eve’s courage, conviction, and deep commitment to the Land of Israel.

Eve is often chosen to guide high-level political leaders and businesspeople, and for good reason. She brings knowledge, insight, and personal relationships that make an experience of Israel truly memorable. When choosing a guide, you really do get what you pay for, and Eve is someone you would be wise to contact.

Beyond her extraordinary knowledge, Eve is a bridge-builder who helps people understand that Judea and Samaria are not simply places on a map. They are the historic and Biblical heartland of Israel, filled with real people, families, and stories that deserve to be heard. Visit EveHarow.com to learn more about Eve and her work.

list.name: Luke Hilton
list.summary: HaYovel’s Director of Marketing. Work includes The Joshua and Caleb Report and The Israel Guys podcast.
story: I first met Luke in early 2018. Glenn Beck was hosting HaYovel for a birthday celebration for the State of Israel. If memory serves, we had 31 people sleeping at our home that week. I quickly recognized this young man was a Divine Appointment, not only for the Wallers’ daughter, but it was clear he was gifted in so many business ways, a perfect fit for the work of HaYovel.

He is now in Israel most of the time as HaYovel’s Director of Marketing, and under his gifted hands, HaYovel has gained international airtime for the popular TV show The Joshua and Caleb Report: Stories from the Heartland of Israel, and now again with Joshua Waller on the popular podcast, The Israel Guys. Sign up for this weekly podcast! I continually find people... Jews and Christians listening to The Israel Guys and not knowing these two men are in the Waller Family!

list.name: Lori Hinze
list.summary: Leads immersive tours focused on the land’s rejuvenation, food, and cultural connection.
story: Lori’s first trip to Israel was in 2014. She had an encounter that changed her life. After that, she began to make multiple trips and even began to lead her own.

The Land stood barren for most of 2000 years, but when the Jews returned, the mountains began to bring forth grapes for wine, and even in an arid region and sometimes even in sand, flowers, fruits, and every type of vegetable began to flourish! Lori believes that the five senses can experience prophecy, especially tasting! For more information on her tours, go to A Taste of Israel. You will not only meet our mutual friends, but you will also have the trip of a lifetime while enjoying every culinary delight the Land has to offer! In 2022 she spent six weeks searching for the best sites for her fall 2023 trip.

Years ago, we became friends because of our kindred spirit of building relationships with no agenda but friendship with the Jewish people. In late 2021 we became partners. Because of COVID, Lori suggested we go visit our friends by Zoom. I have enough trouble with emails or my phone; I could have never even remotely attempted that, but it changed our lives. She is our “adopted daughter,” and we love her! Lori has a great future ahead!

list.name: Mike Isley
list.summary: Founder and president of Texans for Israel, and Vice President of Texans for a Safe Israel.
story: The founder and president of Texans for Israel. Mike is loved by so many in Israel, as well as America. Mike is legendary! We all have a “Mike story”! God has given him the gift and the assignment of being a heavenly connector. With the people Mike meets and the connections he makes, one can only say, “it is the Hand of God.”

Mike knows just about everyone on this list, and a good portion he introduced to me! What is precious about Mike is that he is eager to share these connections with others because he is one who does not care who gets the credit as long as the job gets done! My kids (in their 40s and 50s) call him “Momma’s little brother.” When there is going to be an event, I can count on Mike to either fly or drive to our home to help!

He lives in the Panhandle of Texas. He is such a dear friend. We are both usually up long before the sun rises. He is in Amarillo, and I am in Granbury. Sometimes I will get a text “are you up,” or I’ll text him the same thing. On those days, we have coffee and solve all the world’s problems before sunrise. Do I love this guy... absolutely, like the brother I never had!

list.name: The Israel Guys
list.summary: Biblical news analysis and frontline reporting from Judea and Samaria. Broadcast from the Granbury home during the June 2025 Judea Samaria Convention.
story: The Israel Guys have, to the best of my knowledge, all visited our home in Granbury, Texas.

In June 2025, terrorist threats forced the cancellation of their major U.S. event at the Convention Center in Arlington, Texas, an event showcasing Judea and Samaria. People had already begun arriving from around the world, including from both the East and West Coasts. I especially remember one totally blind man from Canada who had traveled by train, only to learn that the event had been canceled. The Israel Guys brought him out to our home, too.

Fortunately, our home has a theater room, and within just a few days, they transformed it into a first-class newsroom! Although the in-person Judea Samaria Convention could not proceed as planned, the event continued virtually, allowing its important message to reach people despite the threats. Meanwhile, many Israelis were already in town, so our home was filled to capacity, with every bed and couch occupied! It was an extraordinary time of opening our home and doing what we could to help.

I encourage you to check out The Israel Guys’ very popular YouTube channel, featuring biblical news analysis and frontline reporting from Israel. Their work offers a valuable perspective on the people, places, and events shaping the Biblical Heartland of Judea and Samaria. By the way, all this grew out of one family, the Tommy Waller Family, and the establishment of HaYovel.

list.name: Becky Janel
list.summary: Guest Services representative for God’s Learning Channel. Arranges remote interviews from the Granbury home with GLC in West Texas.
story: Becky has been a longtime friend and supporter of TFSI. She lives in a nearby town, Glen Rose, Texas, a charming country-western town much like Granbury. As the Guest Services representative for God’s Learning Channel (GLC) in Odessa, Texas, she plays an important role in connecting guests with the network.

Over the years, Becky has faithfully supported TFSI and, whenever her schedule allows, joins us at our events. She also helps arrange remote interviews from our home with the GLC offices in West Texas, giving our guests another opportunity to share their stories and perspectives with a wider audience.
We are grateful for Becky’s friendship, her continued support of TFSI, and the many ways she helps us share the stories of those who have a heart for Israel.

list.name: Shumel Junger
list.summary: A Sabra and leader with CFOIC, connecting Jewish and Christian communities.
story: Shmuel is with Christian Friends of Israeli Communities. We had the honor of hosting him last year. He was just a joy, and we had the blessing of him coming back in April of this year.

He is a sabra, and he pointed out that of all the Israeli guests we have had... he is the only sabra (Jew born in Israel). To my amazement, besides the children of our guests, he was right! Through CFOIC you can follow Shmuel from community to community.

He also amazed me with the fact that many of the Jews in these communities never heard of Christians who would be a blessing to the Jews. Hard for them to believe, as they have known no Christians that loved the Jews.

list.name: Judy Freeman Kadish
list.summary: Director of Americans for a Safe Israel. AFSI Chizuk Missions are how many of these friendships began.
story: The Director of Americans for a Safe Israel. For several years, Judy was co-director with her mother, Helen Freedman. Judy knows all the “movers and shakers” in the Sovereignty Movement, other Israeli organizations, and their counterparts in America.

This organization changed my life so dramatically in 2011 and continues to do so. You can have no better connection than Judy! AFSI goes twice a year on a Chizuk Mission... once is never enough... you will want to go with them yearly or even twice a year. I met most of the people on this list through Americans for a Safe Israel.
A Holocaust Survivor once told me, “If you go on one of their trips, it will be a trip like no other!” He was right!

list.name: David Kiern
list.summary: Filmmaker behind the short film I Am Israel. Brought to the Stacy home by Mike Isley.
story: A few years ago, Mike Isley brought David Kiern to our home. We showed the now famous short film, I AM ISRAEL. I thought, “someday we will say David Kiern slept here.”

He is a very talented young man with a passion and a love for the Land of Israel and the Jewish People. That love and respect for the Jewish people transfer when he films Eretz Israel and connects the viewer’s hearts to the Promises of God.

list.name: James (Poppa) and Louann Knight
list.summary: Visited the home and left a hand-printed Esther Scroll that the family still keeps.
story: This couple came to our home a few years ago. I remember exactly where he was sitting. Such a sweet man and a lovely wife. They have been to several of our events in Granbury and Keller.

A few weeks after our initial meeting, he called and asked if they could stop by to give me something. My response was, “of course!” That something was a beautiful hand-printed Esther Scroll. Never have I or we been given such a costly and beautiful gift. We certainly didn’t deserve it, but we cherish it. They are two of the nicest people you will ever meet.

list.name: Dr. Ryan Lambert
list.summary: Twenty years in Jewish–Christian relations, focused on the Jewishness of Jesus and Paul.
story: Dr. Ryan Lambert is a Jewish leader who has worked in the area of Jewish-Christian relations for 20 years. He specializes in communicating the Jewishness of Jesus and Paul. As “Your Jewish Coach,” Ryan also helps individuals and organizations find clarity in their passion, purpose and messaging.
Ryan brought a life changing message to me a few years ago on the Jewishness of Paul.

list.name: Dr. Rusty Maisel and John Sliffe
list.summary: Rusty founded The Enduring Word Museum and was an authority on historical manuscripts and early printing. John Sliffe carries on his work.
story: Rusty was one of our first guests at The Blessing in 2015. He founded The Enduring Word Museum in the 1990s and was passionate about helping Christians understand the history of their Bible. He was a recognized authority on historical manuscripts, manuscript traditions, and early printing. I could hardly believe the authentic historical artifacts he brought into our home!
Rusty’s passion extended beyond the Bible itself to Israel and the Jewish people, and he participated in a number of archeological digs. He remained a dear friend until his death in 2022.

John Sliffe has carried on Rusty’s work through The Enduring Word Museum. John lives in the Fort Worth area and travels widely, teaching the fascinating story of how the Bible we know today came into existence. His presentations also explore the history of written communication and the lives of important historical figures who helped bring the Bible to English-speaking audiences, including Johannes Gutenberg, John Wycliffe, William Tyndale, Martin Luther, Miles Coverdale, and King James.

For those interested in learning more about the remarkable history of the Bible and the people who helped make it accessible to generations of readers, John is a wonderful resource. You can contact John Sliffe at jsliffe101@gmail.com.

list.name: Ruthy Mann
list.summary: Runs an animal-assisted therapy ranch in the Judean Hills near Alon, helping Israelis carrying the trauma of war. Visited The Blessing in June 2025.
story: Ruthy Mann operates an animal-assisted therapy center, known as Ruthy’s Horse Farm or Ruti’s Farm, in the Judean Hills near the biblical Good Samaritan Road, east of Jerusalem, outside Alon in the Binyamin region. Ruthy came to The Blessing in June 2025, at the same time as Ayala Bar-On. With so many Israelis carrying the emotional wounds and trauma of war, her therapeutic horses are in great demand. Through her work, Ruthy offers a special kind of healing, helping people find comfort, connection, and hope through their time with these beautiful animals.

There is a lovely short video from CBN that tells Ruthy’s story and gives a glimpse into her important work. Ruthy’s CBN story also connects with the Wallers and The Israel Guys, whose cowboy spirit and practical help have been part of the support surrounding her work.

list.name: Dr. Robert and Janet Mawire
list.summary: Overnight guests. Dr. Mawire worked closely with Ron Nachman, the longtime mayor of Ariel, and twice carried a warning to Benjamin Netanyahu not to divide the Land.
story: Dr. Robert Mawire and his wife, Janet, have both been overnight guests in our home, and I have a remarkable story to share about Dr. Mawire.

As I remember it, Dr. Mawire had worked closely with Ron Nachman, the longtime mayor of Ariel, Samaria. During Benjamin Netanyahu’s first period as Prime Minister, Dr. Mawire believed he had received a word from God specifically for him. He asked Ron Nachman to arrange a meeting with Netanyahu. The message was direct: If you divide the Land, God will remove you from office. As the story was told, Netanyahu smiled and responded with a thought about how false prophets were treated in Israel.

In the years that followed, Netanyahu was voted out of office, and the familiar land for peace process continued, with portions of the Land being surrendered in the hope of achieving peace. Several years later, Dr. Mawire believed he had received another word from the Lord. Once again, he turned to his good friend Ron Nachman to help arrange a meeting with Netanyahu. This time, the reception was more cordial. The message was different, but the warning remained: God would restore Netanyahu to the position of Prime Minister, but he must not divide God’s Land.

I have always found this story compelling. Whether one agrees with every detail of my account or not, it reflects Dr. Mawire’s deep conviction that the Land of Israel is not merely a political issue, but a matter of divine promise and responsibility. It is a story I remember because it brings together faith, friendship, leadership, and the enduring question of what it means to be entrusted with the Land of Israel.

Dr. Mawire has ministered on every continent and is well respected in Evangelical circles. To me personally he is the best ENCOURAGER to individuals that I have ever met. To contact: robertmawire.com and wrno@outlook.com

list.name: Joseph Mendez
list.summary: A world-class violinist who moved to Israel in 2005 to minister to the families expelled from Gaza.
story: Joseph Mendez, The Jerusalem Violinist, a world-class violinist, has such an interesting story. Like many of us, when he fell in love with the Word of G-d, he fell in love with Israel and the Jewish people.

In 2005, when the Jewish families in Gaza were violently expelled from their homes, he moved to Israel to minister to hundreds of refugees scattered throughout the land. His anointed music became like a Balm of Gilead to their broken hearts. He knows all the old Jewish folk songs as well as their modern music. He has been a guest at our home a number of times.

list.name: Charles and Sharon Michaels
list.summary: Met at an AIPAC meeting in Dallas. Sharon has become the face of Israel365 in the Dallas–Fort Worth area.
story: As with so many of the connections TFSI has made over the years, our relationship with Charles and Sharon Michaels seems to have begun by sheer chance, but we have come to recognize how meaningful these unexpected connections can be!

Several years ago, before TFSI even existed, I attended an enormous AIPAC meeting in Dallas, with thousands of people in attendance. Among that sea of people, one man caught my attention. He was walking around wearing a cardboard sign on his hat that read, “Bring Caroline Glick to Dallas!” I immediately stopped him and asked if I could sign up. (Caroline Glick is an American-born conservative journalist, author, and political advisor, and as of today, October 2026, an advisor to Netanyahu.)

I also told Charles Michaels about an upcoming event organized by Glenn Beck to celebrate Israeli Independence Day, featuring our good friends from HaYovel. Later, out of all the thousands of people at that AIPAC gathering, my husband and I “just happened to walk past their table.” Charles looked at me and said, “My wife has already signed up and bought a table for the Glenn Beck event!” And so, another unexpected connection began!
