We became family after that.

In 2022, Rabbi Eli Mischel and Israel Glass from Israel365 came to visit us. They asked whether we could recommend someone in the Jewish community whom they might meet. I suggested Sharon Michaels. Sharon often laughs that she was simply hosting them for coffee, but they were so impressed that they hired her! Since then, Sharon has become the face of Israel365 throughout the Dallas-Fort Worth area and a model for how the organization can develop relationships and expand its reach in other cities.

We often share Israeli guests, and it is always a special joy and great honor to welcome Charles and Sharon as our overnight guests. What began with an unexpected encounter among thousands of people has grown into a valued friendship and a wonderful partnership in our shared love for Israel.

list.name: Lily Sironi Mills
list.summary: Once a high-school attendee at pro-Israel gatherings in the home. Later served with the Israeli Ambassador at the U.N.
story: In high school, she would come to our home in Keller (a suburb of Fort Worth) and listen to pro-Israel Christians and Zionist Jews. Early on, her parents’ lives and ours crossed through Eagle Mountain Church and Tova Feldman, a Hebrew teacher and a Holocaust Survivor. Julie and Ethan were determined to take their very young children on that first trip to Israel.

Watching this young lady graduate high school, graduate university in Israel, and become associated with stellar Orthodox institutions such as Aish HaTorah has been such a joy. She recently married and now works at the U.N. as an aide to the Israeli Ambassador to the U.N.
Look for her one-minute clip, Light Up The Church, and her interview on an Israeli news channel. She did a wonderful job. This is just the beginning for Lily!

list.name: Bob O’Dell
list.summary: A hi-tech entrepreneur and philanthropist from Austin. Author and speaker on Jewish and Israel-related causes.
story: Bob is a good friend who lives in Austin, Texas. I have heard many life testimonies, but Bob’s is one of the best. He is a hi-tech entrepreneur and a philanthropist to Jewish and Israel-related causes.

Bob is also the author of several books; my favorites are The List, The Persecution of Jews by Christians Throughout The Centuries, and Five Years with Orthodox Jews. Bob is another wonderful speaker! This man is a premiere bridge builder!
Bob still teaches Sunday school at his local Methodist Church. To me, that is very important; Bob O’Dell is a LIGHT to the Christian world. We hope to host Bob in the coming months.

list.name: Allan Parker
list.summary: His Justice Foundation played the leading legal role in overturning Roe v. Wade and Doe v. Bolton. Host of the Jerusalem Prayer Breakfast in Dallas and Houston.
story: Allan Parker’s The Justice Foundation played the leading legal role in the case that ultimately helped overturn Roe v. Wade and Doe v. Bolton, two landmark decisions that had established a constitutional right to abortion in America. What an honor it is to know this man and the work of his foundation!

Allan is also a great friend of Israel and has been a gracious host to hundreds of people attending the Jerusalem Prayer Breakfast in both Dallas and Houston. He is also a supporter of other Jerusalem Prayer Breakfasts in the United States as well as foreign countries. The Jerusalem Prayer Breakfast is a wonderful bridge-building initiative, bringing together Jewish government, military, and religious leaders with Christian pastors and their congregations to pray for the peace of Jerusalem and strengthen Jewish-Christian relationships.

A few years ago I purchased Allan’s book, Reversing Roe v. Wade: My Journey with Roe, Doe and God. After reading it, I bought additional copies to share with others. We all might be surprised about the women we know that have the painful memory of an abortion. I encourage you to read this important story and consider giving the book to others. What an honor it is to know this man and his work.

list.name: Elie Pieprz
list.summary: A Jerusalem-based lobbyist in economic policy and taxation and a director of political campaigns. Visited The Blessing in 2025.
story: Elie Pieprz was one of those Divine Appointments for TFSI. Mike Isley of Texans for Israel and I were sitting at the airport getting ready to board a plane for Israel when Elie called Mike. He wanted to let him know that he was coming to the U.S. the next week. Mike told him we were coming to Israel! We met at his home in Jerusalem.

Mike knew him through events with the Republican Party. He was a lobbyist in the field of economic policy and taxation, as well as a director of political campaigns in various countries including the U.S. He is also a graduate of Yeshiva University, as are Rabbi Eli Mischel, Rabbi Yishai Fleisher, Rabbi Jeremy Gimpel, and Rabbi Tuly Weisz, and I am sure more that I just can’t remember right now.
We were so glad that he came to The Blessing to visit us in 2025! We hope to see him again soon!

list.name: Marc Provisor
list.summary: Met in Israel with AFSI. Head of security for One Israel Fund; now also an artist. Artwork at marcpro.art.
story: I met Marc on my first visit to Israel with Americans for a Safe Israel. Early morning on the first day, we went to a hilltop in Samaria where a small family lived in an old bus. They were growing some produce on the rocky ground, and a bedsheet with the star of David was their flag. What amazed me was their happiness in being in Eretz Israel, in living out the prophesied Scriptures about the return of the Jewish people to the Land.

From there, we saw another hilltop community that the army had just demolished because of pressure from the U.S. regarding “illegal building.” It was government land, and only the forces outside of Israel pushed their hand to demolish this little community. From there, we visited the community of Itamar and the very recent tragic event of the murders of the Fogel Family, parents, and their three little children.

There is much to say about Marc. If he is available, he is always included in the Americans for a Safe Israel mission. Marc has the distinction of being in more firefights than anyone else in Israel and surviving. If memory serves, it is near 100. He is the head of security for One Israel Fund. You can contact him through them.

Marc is trying to retire and become the artist he was trained to be in his early life. I recently bought a print from him to give to a Christian ministry that has been very supportive of Judea and Samaria. The backstory to the print is that a few years before, he had forwarded a picture of him and his family (all IDF soldiers) standing under the Arch of Titus in Rome. If you are familiar with it, you know it depicts the Jews in chains and Temple treasures in their arms being carried away to Rome. He mentioned that he had his children with him and told them that it has been 2000 years since the Jewish State had existed with a Jewish army... but now they are back!
For more, go to OneIsraelFund.org, a wonderful organization that fills in the security and social welfare gaps in Judea and Samaria, a worthy cause to donate to.

list.name: David Rose
list.summary: Visited twice — first with ZAKA, later with the Israel Magen Fund, which supports vulnerable communities in the Binyamin region.
story: He has visited our home twice, once with ZAKA, which he represented for years, and later with Israel Magen Fund. This latest organization works round-the-clock to support vulnerable Israeli communities and families living in the Binyamin Region of Israel.
He has overseen the management and funding of thousands of life-saving and recovery projects throughout Israel for over 20 years.

list.name: David Rubin
list.summary: Former mayor of Shiloh and founder of the Shiloh Israel Children’s Fund. Photographed at the house with Ann Stacy.
list.photoAlt: Ann Stacy and David Rubin beneath the Israeli flag in the lodge

list.name: Judy Tashbook Safern
list.summary: Former publisher of Dallas Jewish Monthly, now in Jerusalem. Organized the TFSI campaign that fed Israeli battalions.
story: Formerly the publisher of Dallas Jewish Monthly, Judy is a writer and literary publicist who lives in Jerusalem. She welcomes you to visit her in Israel and to join her family for Shabbos or Jewish holidays.
I first met Judy through the Michaels. Judy was the go-between to bring Caroline Glick to Dallas. She is a chef in her own right and once had a kosher catering business.

Before she moved to Israel, she stayed with us. We had several classes that people loved. One was how to make challah. Judy brought 5 pounds of flour for each person and the biggest bowls I have ever seen as her gift for each person, as well as all the other ingredients. We all treasure those times. One week we did Matza Ball Soup! She is quite a cook, among other things! Judy is a great connector.

list.name: Maura Schreier-Fleming
list.affiliation: TFSI Advisory Board / Israel Now Forum
list.summary: TFSI Advisory Board member and Speakers Chairman of the Israel Now Forum, which holds monthly webinars on Israel and the U.S.–Israel relationship. Founder of Best@Selling.
story: Maura Schreier-Fleming has been a dear friend for several years, and I have come to appreciate not only her friendship but also her heart for building relationships between Christians and the Jewish community. As a member of the Texans for a Safe Israel (TFSI) Advisory Board, Maura has been outstanding in helping us develop meaningful, lasting connections within the Jewish community. She understands that bridge building is about more than supporting a cause; it is about getting to know people, earning trust, and nurturing friendships that grow stronger with time. I am grateful for the role she plays in helping TFSI strengthen these important relationships.

Maura is also an active volunteer, currently serving as Speakers Chairman of the Israel Now Forum (IsraelNowForum.org). Through the forum’s monthly webinars, she helps educate the public on why supporting Israel is good for both Israel and America. By bringing knowledgeable speakers and audiences together, she creates opportunities for people to learn, ask questions, and develop a deeper understanding of Israel and the importance of the U.S.–Israel relationship.

As founder of Best@Selling (BestAtSelling.com), Maura works with business and sales professionals to improve sales and increase productivity. She is the author of Real-World Selling for Out-of-this-World Results and Monday Morning Sales Tips. An engineer by training, she has appeared on numerous radio shows to discuss sales and business. Her clients have included Fujitsu, UPS, BBVA Compass Bank, Ebby Halliday, and the Houston Texans.

Maura’s commitment to service extends well beyond her professional career. Her volunteer leadership has included serving as president of her homeowners association in 2015 and from 2017 through 2021, Speaker Committee Chair for the 2025 Israel Now Forum, and chairman of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Dallas Consultants Network.

I value Maura as a friend who puts her abilities and relationships to work for something bigger than herself. Whether she is connecting people through the Israel Now Forum or helping TFSI strengthen ties with the Jewish community, she brings professionalism, dedication, and a genuine desire to make a difference. For me, Maura represents what bridge building is all about: turning shared support for Israel into personal relationships, mutual understanding, and lasting friendships. Below are some of the Israel Now Forum programs and speakers.
Dr. Jonathan Schanzer, Executive Director, Foundation for Defense of Democracies: “Who Is Really Behind the Protests at U.S. Campuses”
Dr. Mordechai Kedar, International Expert of Arab and Islamic Culture and Researcher, Bar-Ilan University: “Middle Eastern Insights”

Dr. Asaf Romirowsky, Executive Director, Scholars for Peace in the Middle East (SPME) and the Association for the Study of the Middle East and Africa (ASMEA): “October 7th: The Wars Over Words and Deeds”
Jason Wolf, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, Iron Nation: “From Startup Nation to Iron Nation”
Olga Deutsch, Vice President, NGO Monitor: “Analysis of NGOs Claiming to Advance Human Rights”
David Litman, Committee for Accuracy in Middle East Reporting and Analysis (CAMERA): “Fighting Israel’s Misrepresentation in the Media”
Karen Paikin Barall, Chief Policy Officer, The Louis D. Brandeis Center for Human Rights Under Law: “Fighting Antisemitism Through Law and Policy”
Rev. Dr. Tricia Miller, Director, Partnership of Christians and Jews, CAMERA: “Christian Zionists: How Zionism Is Good for Christians and Jews”
Rebecca Schgallis, Director of the K-12 Program, CAMERA: “Turning Back the Red/Green Alliance: Seizing the Reins of Power”
David Collins, George Washington University Program on Extremism: “Hamas in the United States”
Benjamin Baird, Director, MEF Action, Middle East Forum: “Leading the Counter-Islamist Strategy: Grassroots Advocacy”

list.name: Yifa Segal
list.summary: Hosted during a short visit with Judy Kadish. Had recently become Chief of Staff for Gilad Erdan, then Israeli Ambassador to the U.S. and the U.N.
story: It was a pleasure hosting Yifa during her short vacation with our mutual friend, Judy Kadish, Director of Americans for a Safe Israel. Yifa, who had recently moved to Washington as Chief of Staff for Gilad Erdan, the Israeli Ambassador to the U.S. and the U.N., engaged in thought-provoking discussions, including the impact of being a Third Generation Holocaust Survivor, a topic often overlooked by Christians.

list.name: Dr. Tim and Virginia Shepherd
list.summary: Close friends for more than a decade. They connected TFSI with Diane and Jerry Benjamin and are well known for their faithfulness to Jewish causes.
story: Dr. Tim and Virginia Shepherd have been close friends for more than a decade. They were instrumental in connecting us with Diane and Jerry Benjamin, friendships that have become so meaningful to TFSI. It was also through Virginia’s thoughtful proposal that I was honored years ago by B’nai Zion, a Jewish charitable organization.

Over the years, we have shared guests, introduced one another to new people, and opened our homes through these mutual friendships. Tim and Virginia are well known throughout the Jewish community for their unwavering faithfulness to Jewish causes. We are grateful for their friendship and for the many ways they have helped strengthen the relationships between TFSI and the Jewish community.
One last thought... If a new Israeli calls... I always ask... “have you met the Shepherds?”

list.name: Ethan and Julie Sironi
list.summary: Dinner guests whose love for Israel and the Jewish people has influenced the TFSI family and work.
story: They have not stayed with us but have often been at our dinner table. Ethan has had such a positive influence on one of our children’s lives, and in our business life, he has been more than a blessing.

Julie will forever hold a place in my heart for her love for Israel and the Jewish People. I have personally watched Julie for over a decade. The transformation from that housewife who deeply desired to go to Israel to who she is today... astounding. All I can say is she is a God gifted connector with the Jewish people and she is a profound blesser of Israel. In her life... there is so much more to come! The end of that Sironi book has not been written!

list.name: Colonel John Sommerville and Mary
list.summary: John has led Israel trips since 2009. Author of The Accidental Presidents Who Became Blessers of Israel.
story: John is one of the first people I heard speak about Israel. I had driven to Weatherford, Texas in 2009 but was so shy I wouldn’t even go up to talk to him after the event. Years later, I took one of my sons on his Zion’s Watchmen trip.

If you have never been to Israel and you are a Christian, he would be a good one to contact. He and Mary lead several trips a year. John is also an author and an excellent speaker! He has written several books, but my favorite is THE ACCIDENTAL PRESIDENTS WHO BECAME BLESSERS OF ISRAEL.

list.name: Natalie Sopinsky
list.summary: A Delaware native who now lives in Susya, the furthest southern community in Judea. TFSI has helped with needs in Susya.
story: Natalie Sopinsky has become a good friend. TFSI has helped Natalie with needs in Susya, her home in Israel, the furthest southern community in Judea.

According to her website, Natalie is a Delaware native who grew up in an “all-American” Conservative Jewish home. Today, she is a pistol-packing, hitchhiking settler living in the Hebron Hills! What a journey! Natalie’s story is honest, touching, and absolutely fascinating.

She went to Hebrew school and celebrated her bat mitzvah with a big party, but beyond that, she had little connection to her Jewish heritage. She had never been to Israel and had no particular interest in going. Her world revolved around ballet, music, cheerleading, and boys!

You simply have to connect with Natalie and hear her story for yourself. Years ago, we had a website called JUST AMONG FRIENDS, where we featured three 15-minute interviews with Natalie, filmed right in our home. You can find them on YouTube. Natalie is a true heroine and pioneer, and her story is one you won’t want to miss. Be sure to type Natalie Sopinsky into the YouTube search bar along with JUST AMONG FRIENDS. You will be glad you did!

list.name: Kimberly Troop
list.summary: American representative for CFOIC and a mentor in Jewish–Christian relations since 2011.
story: A pioneer in Jewish-Christian relations, Kimberly has been a mentor to me since 2011. As the American representative for Christian Friends of Israeli Communities, her insights have deepened my understanding of Israel’s history and fostered friendship between our communities.

list.name: Dror Vanunu
list.summary: An early visitor who represented Gush Katif refugees and spoke about the cost of land concessions.
story: One of our first visitors. He was the spokesperson for the Gush Katif Refugees. If you know nothing about the refugees, I highly recommend you google Gush Katif. Removing Jews from their homes is one of the ugliest parts of the State of Israel’s history. He was a young, articulate, and attractive man. They couldn’t have picked a better spokesperson. Again, I would like you to learn about this story.

What has come out of the horror of Gush Katif is that the Israelis realize there will be no peace in giving away land. Anita Tucker, “the Celery Lady,” remarked they were escorted by Ariel Sharon to Gaza after the Six-Day War. He told them... “make the desert bloom.”

I remember her telling us an old Arab came to their home and offered bread and olive oil. He said, you are welcome here, but the land is cursed; nothing will grow here; there is nothing but sand. How wrong he was! Google Anita Tucker, The Celery Lady, for an interview by Eve Harow.

list.name: Tommy and Sherri Waller
list.summary: Left successful careers for the mountains of Israel. HaYovel greens the land and brings Christians into the harvest.
story: All of HaYovel is our close family. I have even thought about having “Waller” written on one of our bedroom doors. If there is ever a time to take my shoes off and be myself, it is with our Tennessee family. As with so many of the people on this list, I have seen God grow them and their influence. About 6 or 7 years ago, I told my husband, “Tommy Waller will someday visit our home.” Little did we know that we’d end up giving him a key!

Today their name is synonymous with Judea and Samaria, with the greening of the Mountains of Israel, the grape harvest, tree planting, and the winter pruning. They have eleven children, all but three are married, and as of this month, there are 41 grandchildren! HaYovel is an experience for Christians like none other because it lets Christians connect with the Land through volunteer programs. You have the opportunity to see Biblical prophecy being fulfilled and can be part of that.

Just a few words about Tommy and Sherri. They both left successful careers to live off the grid for six years in an Amish Community. Not an ordinary life, and for sure, these two were made for each other. In 2004 Tommy went to Israel for the first time, saw the vineyards, and read the Biblical Prophecies about the Mountains of Israel coming to life. It wasn’t long before the entire family lived in The Mountains of Israel.
Because of Tommy’s close relationship with the Jewish people, he can articulate to Christians the unique role God has given the Jewish People in the Nation of Israel. Many YouTube videos abound.

list.name: Zac Waller
list.summary: From Tennessee to Israel’s heartland. Executive Director of HaYovel.
story: We met Zac when he came for the Mercury One Event at Glenn Beck studios a few years back.

Zac Waller was born in Kentucky and raised in the hills of Tennessee, but he found his life calling on the mountains of Samaria in the heartland of re-born Israel. At the age of thirteen, he dedicated his life to the God of Israel and professed Yeshua (Jesus) as his Lord and Savior. Little did he know that this commitment would lead him to a thriving vineyard on the Mount of Blessing in Samaria.

During the grape harvest of 2007, the call was made clear: Almighty God was resurrecting the land and people of Israel, and the nations needed to participate! That following year, in recognition of his managerial giftings that had blossomed while farming with his family in Tennessee, HaYovel’s Board of Directors voted him in as its Director. After six years of much growth and success, Zac was promoted to the position of Executive Director. He is married to the beautiful Becca and has at least six children at this writing!

list.name: David Wilder
list.summary: Former English spokesperson for the Jewish community of Hebron. A pivotal voice in TFSI’s understanding of Hebron.
story: God has sent me many Divine Appointments, but this man stands at the top of the list. About David, and his wife Ora, I could write a book.

One of my most treasured memories was spending Chayei Sarah with them in their home. My room had a bullet hole through the wall that they later creatively used to run a wire to the outside. His library had books with bullet holes in them.

He was the English Spokesperson for the Jewish Community of Hebron for 22 years, 22 very difficult years for Hebron. He imparted in my heart not only a love for Hebron but also the history of what this ancient city has gone through.

Because I was with Religious Zionists, we always were in Hebron for Chayei Sarah. On a whim, in recent years, I looked up what Torah portion I was born under in 1948. To my amazement, I was actually born on a Shabbat of Chayei Sarah.
At the beginning of my journey in Jewish-Christian relations, I cannot tell you how alone I felt. However, God sent me David Wilder, who became my first Jewish mentor.

list.name: Steve Wilhite
list.summary: EVP of Daystar. Particular care for Orthodox and Religious Zionist communities.
story: The Executive Vice President of Daystar Christian TV. My husband and I first met Steve 25+ years ago when Daystar was in its infancy. We have seen it grow into the largest Christian Network in the World. He is a “behind-the-scenes” man, but Daystar would not be where they are today had it not been for Steve Wilhite.

One of the greatest honors we have ever received was a call from Steve on the day of Marcus Lamb’s funeral. He asked if we would come and sit with him and his wife. No one loves Israel or the Jewish people, especially the Orthodox Jewish people, the Religious Zionists, more than Steve Wilhite. He has been a blessing in our lives for so many years!

list.name: Jack Wilson
list.summary: Stopped the gunman at West Freeway Church of Christ in December 2019. Now Hood County Commissioner for Precinct 3. Helped TFSI send supplies to Israeli soldiers.
story: Jack Wilson was an ordinary citizen of Granbury, Texas, until the morning of December 29, 2019, when his quick action changed the course of a tragic day. During a church service at West Freeway Church of Christ in Fort Worth, Jack fatally shot a gunman who had already killed two people. His courageous response is credited with preventing further casualties among the approximately 250 people present. According to the Texas Rangers, the gunman had enough ammunition to kill many more. That fateful day changed Jack’s life and helped save the lives of countless others, including his own family.

Today, Jack serves as Hood County Commissioner for Precinct 3. A committed conservative, he works diligently to defend Second Amendment rights. Jack is also a passionate friend of Israel and the Jewish people. During the war, he helped Texans For A Safe Israel (TFSI) send supplies to Israeli soldiers, demonstrating that his commitment to protecting others extends far beyond his own community.

One especially meaningful connection came when Rabbi Yehuda Glick was preparing to stay overnight with us at The Blessing. Rabbi Glick, who had barely survived an assassination attempt on his own life in 2014, specifically asked to be introduced to Jack. Their meeting brought together two men whose lives had been forever changed by encounters with deadly violence.

items.title: Meeting critical needs
body: The Monday after the October 7 massacre, before Texas sunrise, TFSI called Jeremy Gimpel. His family and others live at Arugot Farm in the Judean Desert, surrounded by hostile neighbors. He needed a drone — the equivalent of fifty men on watch. The next day it was active. The farm later became a fortress for fifteen mothers and children while their fathers were at war.

items.title: Holocaust survivors
body: Survivors are often the group most wary of the word Christian. The work is kindness without proselytizing: two air conditioners, a refrigerator, washer and dryer, a deep freezer, iPads, phones, computers, a remodeled bathroom, a bread maker for challah, grocery cards at the holidays.
A 92-year-old concert pianist received a piano. If you want more on this work, contact the house and ask.

items.title: Security
body: Since October 7, TFSI has funded drones, bulletproof vests, scopes, cameras, helmets, medical bags, tactical boots, winter jackets, and a hand-warmer campaign. Communities helped include Har Bracha, Chavat Gilad, Arugot Farm, Susya, Itamar, Shiloh, and Homesh.

items.title: Feed the soldiers
body: Donations fed battalions in the field. Judy Tashbook Safern organized and raised most of those funds through tfsi.org — water, Coca-Cola, Red Bull, whatever they asked for.

items.title: Emotional needs
body: Amitsim, headed by Rabbi Yehuda and Hadass Glick, works with young widows and orphans. David Rubin’s Shiloh Israel Children’s Fund works with traumatized children. After October 7, that demand is not shrinking.

items.title: Israel trips
body: The first TFSI trip was May 2023: seven American Christians with nine American Jews from Americans for a Safe Israel. Contact the house for the next one.

items.title: The Biblical Highway
body: One long goal is that Route 60 become known as Israel’s national highway — the Biblical Highway. Rest stops in the Holy Cities, scenic overlooks, tourist information, a restaurant, a hotel. Tourism and Israeli business both change if people can actually travel the spine of the land.

items.title: Young adult influencers
body: Support for Israel is high among retired Americans and drops sharply in younger age groups. TFSI takes young people to the land. A page of those stories is still being built. Until then, the invitation is the same: come to Israel and become an influencer yourself.

items.title: Texas–Israel Embassy
body: A working embassy between the State of Texas and the State of Israel: staffers from Texas in Israel, staffers from Israel in Texas. A place Texans can go for assistance, guides, and recommended travel — and a place for Texas and Israeli businesses to meet.
